senses.gloss:
vaṃśá, m.
 —1. cane or stock or stem, esp.
of the bamboo;
 —2. (like Eng. stock, and
stem [rarely], and Ger. Stamm) lineage,
family, race.

vaṃśa-viśuddha, a.
 —1. made of perfectly
clear or unblemished bamboo;
 —2. of pure lineage. [lit. ‘vanśa-pure,
pure in its or his vaṃśa,’ 1265: √śudh.]

vánanvant, a. having desire, desiring.
[perhaps fr. vanánā, 1233, w. irreg. loss
of final ā: both mg and derivation are
doubtful.]

vana-prastha, m. n. forest-plateau,
wooded table-land. [1280b.]

vānaprastha, m. a Brahman of the
third order, who has passed through the
stages of student and householder (see
āśrama) and dwells in the woods, 65^3N.;
hermit. [vanaprastha: for mg, cf.
ἐρημίτης, Eng. hermit, and ἐρημία, ‘solitude,
 desert.’]

vana-vāsa, m. the living in a wood;
-tas, owing to (his) forest-life.

vánas-páti, m. tree. [‘lord of the
wood’: see 1267 and a and d: perhaps
vanas stands for vanar, a subsidiary
form of vana, cf. 171^3.]
